title: Pink Tulip Hanging Ornament
subtitle: A stuffed crochet tulip with stem and leaf on a beaded cord
finished_size: ≈ 21 cm (8.3 in) plus an 8 cm loop
description: A small stuffed tulip — a cup worked in spiral rounds with three pointed petals, plus an oval front petal — on a tube stem with one leaf, strung with beads above a cream tassel. The cord runs through the stem tube.
glance: ≈ 21 cm (8.3 in) plus an 8 cm loop
size_guide: One size. For a larger ornament use light worsted (#4) cotton and a 3 mm hook; for a smaller one use sport-weight cotton and a 2 mm hook. Beads and tassel length can be changed freely.
gauge: 22 sc and 24 rows/rnds = 10 cm (4 in) in single crochet with a 2.5 mm hook. Gauge is not critical for an ornament, but work firmly so that stuffing does not show and flat pieces keep their shape; sizes depend on your tension.
swatch: Optional density check: ch 12, then work 10 rows of sc on 11 sts. The square should measure about 5 cm (2 in) wide and 4 cm (1.6 in) tall. If it is larger or you see gaps between stitches, use a smaller hook.

materials.detail: DK (#3) cotton, pink — approx. 5 m (6 yd), about 3 g — 1 ball of 50 g (about 115 m) is enough
DK (#3) cotton, sage green — approx. 3 m (4 yd), about 2 g — 1 ball of 50 g (about 115 m) is enough
DK (#3) cotton, cream — approx. 12 m (13 yd), about 5 g — 1 ball of 50 g (about 115 m) is enough
3 gold-tone beads 6 mm (hole at least 2.5 mm); 2 natural wooden beads 12 mm (hole at least 3 mm). Both cord strands must pass through each bead together — test before you start.
fiberfill (a small handful), stitch marker, pins, tapestry needle, stiff card, scissors

abbreviations: work the sequence in brackets N times

techniques.name: Magic ring (MR)
techniques.how: Wrap the yarn twice around two fingers, insert the hook under both strands, pull up a loop and ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). Work the stitches of Rnd 1 over both strands, then pull the tail firmly to close the centre.

techniques.name: Spiral rounds
techniques.how: Do not join or turn. Place a stitch marker in the first stitch of each round and move it up as you go.

techniques.name: sc2tog (flat pieces)
techniques.how: Insert the hook in the next st, yo and pull up a loop; insert in the following st, yo and pull up a loop (3 loops on hook); yo and draw through all 3.

techniques.name: Tassel neck wrap
techniques.how: Lay a 5 cm loop of the wrapping strand along the tassel, pointing down. Wrap the long end tightly around tassel and loop, from the top down. Pass the end through the loop, then pull the short tail at the top until the loop disappears under the wraps. Trim both ends and hide them in the skirt.

notes: Joined rounds (where a round says "Join"): unless the round says otherwise, start the round with ch 1, which does not count as a stitch, and finish it with a sl st into the first stitch.
Right side: for pieces worked in rounds, the outside of the rounds; for pieces worked in rows, choose the neater side and mark it. "Wrong sides together" means the marked right sides face out.
US crochet terms are used throughout.
The number in parentheses at the end of a row or round is the number of stitches you should have when it is finished. Tick the box when you finish each step.
Rows: ch 1 at the start of a row does not count as a stitch; rounds worked in a magic ring are worked in continuous spirals unless the round says "join".
Leave a 20 cm (8 in) tail when you fasten off a piece that will be sewn; weave in all other ends on the wrong side as you go.

blocks.text: The cup is worked in spiral rounds from the bottom; the three pointed petals are then worked in rows on its top edge.

steps.label: Rnd 1
steps.text: With Yarn A, 6 sc in MR.

steps.label: Rnd 2
steps.text: inc x6.

steps.label: Rnd 3
steps.text: (sc 1, inc) x6.

steps.label: Rnd 4
steps.text: sc 1, inc, (sc 2, inc) x5, sc 1.

steps.label: Rnds 5–6
steps.text: sc in each st around (2 rnds). Sl st in the next st; do not fasten off.
Petals: the 24 sts are divided into 3 groups of 8; place a marker in every 8th st so the groups are clear. Each petal is worked in rows over one group.

steps.label: Row 1
steps.text: First petal: ch 1; starting in the same st as the sl st, sc2tog, sc 4, sc2tog over the first group of 8 sts. Ch 1, turn.

steps.label: Row 2
steps.text: sc2tog, sc 2, sc2tog. Ch 1, turn.

steps.label: Row 3
steps.text: sc2tog x2. Ch 1, turn.

steps.label: Row 4
steps.text: sc2tog. Fasten off, leaving a 20 cm tail for sewing.
Second and third petals: join Yarn A with a sl st in the next unworked st of Rnd 6, ch 1 and work Rows 1–4 over the next 8 sts. Repeat once more over the last 8 sts.
Stuff the cup firmly. Using the tails (sew down from each tip), sew the edges of neighbouring petals together along Rows 1–2 only, so the cup closes over the stuffing and the petal tips stay free.

steps.label: Rnd 1
steps.text: With Yarn A, ch 6. Sc in 2nd ch from hook, sc in next 3 ch, 3 sc in last ch; working along the other side of the chain, sc in next 3 ch, 2 sc in the first ch (the same ch as the first sc).

steps.label: Rnd 2
steps.text: inc, sc 3, inc x3, sc 3, inc x2.
ops: inc, sc 3, inc x3, sc 3, inc x2

steps.label: Rnd 3
steps.text: Sl st in each st around, working (sl st, ch 2, sl st) in the 4th of the 6 sts made by the inc x3 at the rounded end (this becomes the top point). Fasten off, leaving a 30 cm tail.

blocks.text: Pin the front petal on the front of the cup, point up, covering the seam between two cup petals, with its lower end 2 rnds above the magic ring. Whipstitch all the way round except the top third, so its tip stands free.

steps.label: Rnd 1
steps.text: With Yarn B, 5 sc in MR.

steps.label: Rnds 2–8
steps.text: sc in each st around (7 rnds). Do not stuff. Fasten off, leaving a 20 cm tail.

steps.label: Leaf
steps.text: With Yarn B, make a chain of 10. Working in the back bumps: sl st in 2nd ch from hook, sc in next ch, hdc in next ch, dc in next 4 ch, hdc in next ch, 3 sc in last ch; working along the other side of the chain: hdc in next ch, dc in next 4 ch, hdc in next ch, sc in next ch, sl st in the last ch (the tip). Fasten off, leaving a 20 cm tail.

blocks.text: Sew the magic-ring end of the stem to the centre of the cup base. Sew the base of the leaf (the 3-sc end) to the side of the stem at Rnd 6, tip pointing up and out; tack the leaf to the stem 1 cm higher so it stays upright.
The tassel is made first: the hanging cord is tied into its top, so the cord runs through the whole ornament and is anchored in the tassel.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.text: Cut a piece of stiff card 10 cm (3.9 in) tall. Wrap Yarn C (cream) around the card 40 times, keeping the wraps side by side and not too tight. Cut the yarn at the bottom edge.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.text: Cut the hanging cord: one 110 cm (43 in) length of Yarn C. Slide it under all the wraps along the top edge of the card so that its middle sits there, and tie it in a tight square knot around the wraps. Both cord ends now point upwards.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.text: Cut through all the wraps along the bottom edge of the card and remove the card. Let the strands hang down from the cord knot.

steps.label: Step 4
steps.text: Tassel neck: cut a 70 cm length of Yarn C. Measure 2 cm down from the top fold and wrap it tightly 8 times around the bundle (see Tassel neck wrap in Techniques).

steps.label: Step 5
steps.text: Trim the skirt evenly to 9 cm (3.5 in) from the top fold. Hold it over steam (or dampen it) and comb the strands straight with your fingers; let it dry hanging.

blocks.title: Pieces at a glance
blocks.caption: Approximate sizes; the cup is stuffed, the other pieces are flat.

items: Thread both cord ends together through a large-eye tapestry needle (or a bead needle with a big eye). Work upwards from the tassel.
String, from the tassel upwards: 1 wooden bead → 1 gold bead → the tulip with its stem → 1 gold bead → 1 wooden bead → 1 gold bead.
Tulip: push the needle up through the open end of the stem tube, through the stem, the cup base and the stuffing, and out between the three petal tips at the top.
Push everything down snugly onto the tassel so there are no gaps. Holding both cord ends together, tie one overhand knot right above the top bead to lock the stack.

Hanging loop: tie the two cord ends together with a square knot so that the loop measures 8 cm (3 in) from the overhand knot to the top. Trim the ends to 5 mm and add a drop of fabric glue to the knot if you like.

blocks.label: Safety
blocks.text: This is a decoration, not a toy, and not suitable for children under 3 years. Beads and cords are a choking and strangling hazard: hang it out of reach of babies, young children and pets.

observations.evidence: Stuffed pink cup with a large oval petal in front and two pointed tips behind
observations.conclusion: Stuffed cup in rounds with 3 petals in rows, plus a sewn-on front petal

observations.evidence: Shows three separate petals sewn into a cup
observations.conclusion: Replaced by one cup piece + front petal (design choice: firmer, easier to stuff)

observations.evidence: Green stem with one leaf on the left
observations.conclusion: 5-st tube stem, leaf worked around a chain

observations.evidence: Cream cord loop above a gold–wood–gold bead stack; same stack below the piece
observations.conclusion: Cord tied into the tassel top and threaded up through beads and piece

observations.evidence: Long full tassel with a rounded head and a wrapped neck
observations.conclusion: Wrapped-card tassel, about 40 wraps, neck wrapped 8 times

accuracy.text: Sizes are scaled from the photo using the 12 mm wooden beads as the reference; the photos look like rendered images, so stitch counts are a design reconstruction, not a count from a real sample. Make the piece once and compare before selling the pattern.

assumptions: Cup and petal counts are a design reconstruction of the photographed shape.

closing_note: Thank you for making this ornament. Happy crocheting!
